newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends up on shortcovering, weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends up on shortcovering, weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended much higher Thursday, carried early by a pipeline problem rumor but supported late by continuing cold in the eastern U.S. and technical selling after breaking through front-month resistance, industry sources said.
December finished 14.2 cents higher at $2.787 per million British thermal units after hitting a high of $2.80 earlier in the session. January settled up 13.8 cents at $2.788.
"We bounced through $2.75. The trend is up. There are some nervous bears out there," said one trader, adding that he thought most traders were uncertain on the market's next move.
Technically, resistance in December, which expires next Thursday, was seen at $2.805, then the $2.88 contract high.
Support in December was first pegged at $2.615, then the $2.53 area.
The 12-month strip rose 5.9 cents to $2.241. NYMEX said an estimated 44,332 Henry Hub contracts traded, up from Wednesday's revised tally of 27,003.

In Thursday's cash market, Gulf Coast prices rose by about one to three cents to the low-to-mid $2.70s, while Midcontinent prices eased into the mid-to-high $2.50s ahead of more seasonable weather this weekend. Prices at the New York city-gate extended its rally as deals were reported done as high as $3.80.
Temperatures in the Northeast are expected to rise to above-normal levels on Monday and Tuesday but then return to below-normal by the middle of next week.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas settled at the contract high of $1.65, up 14 cents from Wednesday's session, led by a rally in the Alberta cash market.

Sources reported closing deals for Friday gas flow at AECO in the low-C$2 per gigajoule area, the highest levels of the year, as cold temperatures were expected to linger through at least this weekend and the West Coast continued to demand large volumes of gas from a tight market.
NYMEX said an estimated 23 Alberta contracts traded.
NYMEX Permian natgas was still untraded for the sixth consecutive day. December settled eight cents higher at $2.53.
Permian cash prices held relatively steady in the low-$2.50s.
On the KCBT, December ended 12.5 cents higher at $2.595, while deferreds were up two to 10 cents at the close. The December East/West spread widened by 1.7 cents to 19.2 cents (NYMEX premium).
Cash prices at Waha were in line with futures in the mid-to-high $2.50s, traders said.
